Turkish vs English

The Text tab's reading questions, in Turkish and in English

547 of the Text tab's 656 reading questions, translated into English, asked of 73 setups (37 decision models and 36 chat model setups), each compared with its own Turkish run.

Sixteen of the 73 setups compared scored higher on the English translation than on the Turkish original; 55 scored lower; two the same; four of the 73 differences are significant after Holm's correction over all 73 English setups: Microsoft-Decision-1 (higher in English), Metask-Jev 4B (higher in English), Liquid d1-2B (open weights) (higher in English) and meraGPT Decider 1 (higher in English) (Paired test).

547 of the Text tab's 656 reading questions, translated into English, asked of 37 decision models, each compared with its own Turkish run.

Twelve of the 37 decision models compared scored higher on the English translation than on the Turkish original; 24 scored lower; one the same; four of the 37 differences are significant after Holm's correction over all 73 English setups: Microsoft-Decision-1 (higher in English), Metask-Jev 4B (higher in English), Liquid d1-2B (open weights) (higher in English) and meraGPT Decider 1 (higher in English) (Paired test).

547 of the Text tab's 656 reading questions, translated into English, asked of 36 chat model setups, each compared with its own Turkish run.

Four of the 36 chat model setups compared scored higher on the English translation than on the Turkish original; 31 scored lower; one the same; none of the differences is significant after Holm's correction over all 73 English setups, so each could be chance (Paired test).

Limit: Claude Opus 5.5 translated the questions and flagged those whose answer depends on Turkish wording. No person checked the translations or the flags, so an error could move a setup's English accuracy (Our method).

Beside the ranking: Web grounding, Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2 (API) against Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2 (API, with web). PWS-Decisions, the decision models on Parallel's benchmark of dated web facts.

Ordered by p, highest first. On the 547 kept reading questions, Liquid d1-ultra's first English run (run 411) against each other decision model's first English run: the exact McNemar test on the questions only one of the two got right, with p adjusted by Holm's method over the 36 decision models. Verdict: too close to call when the Holm-adjusted p is 0.05 or more; otherwise behind d1-ultra when Liquid d1-ultra has more questions only it got right, ahead of it when the other model has more. Each model's name links its model page's English section, as in the tables above; Paired test compares each model with itself in Turkish.

Liquid d1-ultra against each decision model in English is for decision models only.

Ordered by Turkish accuracy, highest first. * marks a difference that is significant after Holm's correction: its paired test (the exact McNemar test, with p adjusted by Holm's method over all 73 English setups) has a Holm-adjusted p below 0.05. Accuracy: right answers over the 547 kept reading questions, the first English run against the Text tab run (Accuracy, Paired test). The “I don't know” columns: each model's first English run with “I don't know” against its Turkish run with the option also written “I don't know” (the Hallucination tab's option-word run, counted on these questions), so only the language differs (Only the language differs). Answered: (right + wrong) / 547; Wrong of answers: wrong / (right + wrong); Non-hallucination: “I don't know” / (“I don't know” + wrong); the difference's paired test is of wrong answers, with p adjusted by Holm's method over the 10 models with both runs. Turkish with “Bilmiyorum”: the Turkish side of the published comparison with “Bilmiyorum” (With “I don't know”) or, for a model outside it, its Hallucination tab run counted on these questions; its wrong of answers with its answered share and non-hallucination rate under it. Not run: no such run for a decision model (the Turkish “I don't know” run is for decision models only); Running: a chat model's run still running. Cost and latency: the Text tab run and the first English run, cost in $ per 1,000 questionsper 1M questions and the median time per request with the request size and the requests in flight under it (Cost, Latency). Rank: by accuracy among the 73 setups in each language, 1 the most accurate, tied setups sharing a rank. Languages: what each model's card or its maker's docs list, with the source (Languages the model cards list); Not checked: no card checked yet. The full tables are under Info.

Costs: API list prices and recorded token use. Setups on our own GPUs: the maker's list price for the same model (each value's tooltip names it); our hardware cost is not measured. On our GPUs, estimated at a public host's list price for the same weights (the host, the date read and any precision difference are on each setup's page): an API-equivalent estimate, not measured spending. On our GPUs with no public price for the same weights, estimated from GPU time: the run's request time x the GPUs its server held x Runpod's on-demand price for an RTX PRO 6000, $2.49 per GPU-hour (read 5 November 2026): a cloud-equivalent estimate, not measured spending. ≤ Upper-bound estimate: one $0.001 web search counted per request; Perplexity bills only completed searches.

Ordered by Turkish accuracy, highest first. * marks a difference that is significant after Holm's correction: its paired test (the exact McNemar test, with p adjusted by Holm's method over all 73 English setups) has a Holm-adjusted p below 0.05. Accuracy: right answers over the 547 kept reading questions, the first English run against the Text tab run (Accuracy, Paired test). The “I don't know” columns: each model's first English run with “I don't know” against its Turkish run with the option also written “I don't know” (the Hallucination tab's option-word run, counted on these questions), so only the language differs (Only the language differs). Answered: (right + wrong) / 547; Wrong of answers: wrong / (right + wrong); Non-hallucination: “I don't know” / (“I don't know” + wrong); the difference's paired test is of wrong answers, with p adjusted by Holm's method over the 10 models with both runs. Turkish with “Bilmiyorum”: the Turkish side of the published comparison with “Bilmiyorum” (With “I don't know”) or, for a model outside it, its Hallucination tab run counted on these questions; its wrong of answers with its answered share and non-hallucination rate under it. Not run: no such run for a decision model (the Turkish “I don't know” run is for decision models only); Running: a chat model's run still running. Cost and latency: the Text tab run and the first English run, cost in $ per 1,000 questionsper 1M questions and the median time per request with the request size and the requests in flight under it (Cost, Latency). Rank: by accuracy among the 37 decision models in each language, 1 the most accurate, tied setups sharing a rank. Languages: what each model's card or its maker's docs list, with the source (Languages the model cards list); Not checked: no card checked yet. The full tables are under Info.

Costs: API list prices and recorded token use. Setups on our own GPUs: the maker's list price for the same model (each value's tooltip names it); our hardware cost is not measured. On our GPUs, estimated at a public host's list price for the same weights (the host, the date read and any precision difference are on each setup's page): an API-equivalent estimate, not measured spending. On our GPUs with no public price for the same weights, estimated from GPU time: the run's request time x the GPUs its server held x Runpod's on-demand price for an RTX PRO 6000, $2.49 per GPU-hour (read 5 November 2026): a cloud-equivalent estimate, not measured spending. ≤ Upper-bound estimate: one $0.001 web search counted per request; Perplexity bills only completed searches.

With an “I don't know” option

The same 547 kept questions with a sixth option, “I don't know” in English and “Bilmiyorum” in Turkish, as on the Hallucination tab, asked of the same models (how).

33 of the 57 models with both runs had a higher non-hallucination rate in English than in Turkish; 24 lower; six of the 57 differences in wrong answers are significant after Holm's correction within each group (decision models, chat models): Liquid d1-2B (open weights) (more wrong answers in Turkish), Laya multilingual (more wrong answers in Turkish), GLiNER2.5 Multi (base) (more wrong answers in Turkish), GLiNER2.5-multi-Decide (more wrong answers in Turkish), Perplexity Decider Flash v1.2 (more wrong answers in Turkish) and Metask-Jev 4B (more wrong answers in Turkish) (Paired test). Celeris-1 Decision has an English rate of 71.3% (92 “I don't know” of 129 not right) with an attempt rate of 83.2% (455 answered) but no Turkish run with “Bilmiyorum” on these questions, so no comparison or test. Still running in Turkish, so charted with one side and in no test: Grok 4.7, GPT-6 Astra (low reasoning, 16 per request), GPT-6 Astra (medium reasoning, 16 per request), GPT-6.1 Sol (low reasoning, 1 per request), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 1017 (reasoning on) and Claude Sonnet 5.5 (high reasoning, 1 per request). Read each rate with its attempt rate: a model that always chose the option would reach 100%.

With the option written “I don't know” in Turkish too, so that only the language differs, the decision models' comparison is in the next section.

With an “I don't know” option

Still running in Turkish, so charted with one side and in no test: Grok 4.7, GPT-6 Astra (low reasoning, 16 per request), GPT-6 Astra (medium reasoning, 16 per request), GPT-6.1 Sol (low reasoning, 1 per request), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 1017 (reasoning on) and Claude Sonnet 5.5 (high reasoning, 1 per request). Only the language differs: “I don't know” in both

The same 547 kept questions with the sixth option written “I don't know” in English and in Turkish too, with the same sentence added to the instructions: each model's first English run with the option, as in the section above, against its Turkish run from the option's word check of the Hallucination tab, counted on these questions. Only the language differs: of the question and its options, of the word in the instructions that names it and of the options heading (how).

Ten of the 37 decision models have both runs. Among them, wrong of answers was lower in English for three and higher for seven; the non-hallucination rate was lower in English for one and higher for nine. None of the 10 differences in wrong answers is significant after Holm's correction over the 10, so each could be chance; the smallest adjusted p is SubQ Snap 1.1's, p = 0.3 (Paired test). English only, with no Turkish run with the option written “I don't know”: Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2 (API, with web), Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2 (API), Liquid d1, Clef, OneJev 27B, Jev 1.14.0, Inception Mercury Decide, Microsoft-Decision-1, Open-Jev 27B v1.1, Celeris-1 Decision, GPT-6 Luna (Decisions API), Cygnet, Winnow-12B, Clef-flash, Perplexity Decider Flash v1.2, Metask-Jev 4B, Liquid d1-2B (open weights), Strands Decider 2B, Laya, GLiNER2.5-multi-Decide and Laya multilingual (in the main table and the table under Info, with no test).

The option's word: “I don't know” instead of “Bilmiyorum”

The Hallucination tab's 2,198 Turkish questions, with the sixth option “Bilmiyorum” and again with “I don't know”, and only the sentence that names it changed: a model that skipped “Bilmiyorum” because it did not recognise the Turkish word should choose “I don't know” more often. Each of the 11 models' first run with each word, in the Hallucination tab's order; the full table and method are on the Hallucination tab.

Answered: (right + wrong) / 2,198 questions. Wrong of answers: wrong / (right + wrong). Both are worked out from the published counts; under each non-hallucination rate, of the 2,198 questions, the right answers, the wrong ones and the option. * marks a difference whose paired test (the exact McNemar test on the questions only one of the two runs got wrong, with p adjusted by Holm's method over the models) has a Holm-adjusted p below 0.05.

Risk and coverage

How often each setup answers and how often its answers are wrong, on the same 547 kept questions in both languages: without the option, by holding back the answers below a confidence score, and with the option, as the model chose it.

Method

Answered = right + wrong (an invalid answer or one without a score is never answered). Coverage = answered / 547. Error rate among answered (risk) = wrong / answered. Abstained: for a run with the option, the times it chose the option; for a confidence point, 547 minus answered minus invalid. Each confidence curve has one point per distinct score of the run on these questions (answer when the score is at least that score; the score is the recorded probability of the chosen option for a decision model and the confidence a chat model stated with its answer): answers with equal scores enter together, so coverage moves in jumps and every point is one the run achieved; a setup that reports its scores with few decimals has many equal scores, so its curve has fewer points, moves in larger steps and can start well above 0% coverage (each curve is drawn from its first point). Every series counts these questions only (a run on the full bank is restricted to them) and is each setup's first run. Turkish curves: the Text tab run; English curves: the first English run. Turkish with “Bilmiyorum” is the Turkish side of the English “I don't know” comparison or, for a model outside it, its Hallucination tab run, restricted to these; Turkish with “I don't know” is the option's word control on the Hallucination tab's questions, restricted to these, for decision models only. A run not yet in reads Not run for a decision model and Running for a chat model.

All series are counted on the same kept reading questions; a full-bank run is restricted to them; first runs only. Answered = right + wrong (an invalid answer or one without a score is never answered). Coverage = answered / kept questions. Risk = error rate among answered = wrong / answered. Abstained: for a native point, the times the model chose the option; for a curve point, kept questions - answered - invalid. A native point is the run with its abstention option (Turkish "Bilmiyorum", Turkish "I don't know" as the wording control, English "I don't know"); Turkish "Bilmiyorum" is the Turkish side of the English "I don't know" comparison or, for a model outside it, its Hallucination tab run; a missing one is Not measured. A curve is one five-option run held back by its recorded score (the probability of the chosen option): one point per distinct score s, answering when the score is at least s; answers with equal scores enter together, so coverage moves in jumps and every point is an achieved one; all distinct points kept, ordered by coverage.

Info The table, the setups without an English run and our method, then the same with “I don't know”

About this test

Since 5 November 2026 every setup of the Text tab also runs in English, decision models and chat models alike, each with its Text tab run's settings and compared with that run. 73 of the Text tab's 79 setups have an English run so far, 37 decision models and 36 chat model setups; the other six are listed under Results with the reason each has none yet. This tab is separate from the leaderboard; it ranks nothing on the Text tab and changes none of its numbers.

The Text tab's reading questions (units 1 to 6; the grammar questions are left out) were translated into English by Claude Opus 5.5. The same model flagged the questions whose answer depends on Turkish wording; the 109 flagged questions are left out and the other 547 kept. Each of the 73 English setups answered the kept questions in English and is compared with its own Text tab run on the same 547 questions.

Download: results.json (the comparison's numbers, under english_reading), answers.json (each English run's answers, under english_runs), english-reading.json (the translator, its prompts, the flags, the question units and each question's hash of its English text; no question text) and kept-question-ids.txt (the 547 kept questions' IDs, one per line).

Results

The setups of the group the view bar shows, ordered by accuracy in English, highest first. Each row compares the setup's first English run with its Text tab run, out of the 547 kept questions; an invalid answer counts as not right. Where a side has more than one run, its accuracy shows the range over its runs and its runs show how many answers changed between them. The paired counts, p and the Holm-adjusted p (over all 73 English setups, whatever the group shown) are those of the exact McNemar test; * marks a Holm-adjusted p below 0.05.

Without an English run

Six of the Text tab's 79 setups have no English run yet, each with its reason:

  • Perplexity Decider 27B v1.1: Perplexity's API now answers requests for v1.1 with v1.2, so a new run could not measure v1.1.
  • Fastino GLiDE: since 10 October, our requests for fastino/GLiDE have been answered by Fastino's glide_v2 engine, not the glide engine of its Turkish run (6 October), so an English run would not measure the same model.
  • DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, first release (reasoning on) and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, first release (reasoning off): they run on our GPUs, which other work holds, and wait for a GPU window; their first-release weights must also be downloaded again, as the server folder now holds the 1017 weights.
  • GLM-5.3-Flash (reasoning on) and GLM-5.3-Flash (reasoning off): they run on all four of our GPUs at once, which other work holds, and wait for a four-GPU window.

Without an English run

Two of the Text tab's 39 decision models have no English run yet, each with its reason:

  • Perplexity Decider 27B v1.1: Perplexity's API now answers requests for v1.1 with v1.2, so a new run could not measure v1.1.
  • Fastino GLiDE: since 10 October, our requests for fastino/GLiDE have been answered by Fastino's glide_v2 engine, not the glide engine of its Turkish run (6 October), so an English run would not measure the same model.

Without an English run

Four of the Text tab's 40 chat model setups have no English run yet, each with its reason:

  • DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, first release (reasoning on) and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, first release (reasoning off): they run on our GPUs, which other work holds, and wait for a GPU window; their first-release weights must also be downloaded again, as the server folder now holds the 1017 weights.
  • GLM-5.3-Flash (reasoning on) and GLM-5.3-Flash (reasoning off): they run on all four of our GPUs at once, which other work holds, and wait for a four-GPU window.

Our method

The translation

The translator is Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5) at effort high; route: Claude Code CLI, Claude subscription, Claude Code version 2.1.312. Its maker has no decision model on our board. Of its maker's chat models, Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5 answered the English questions too, the translator's own model among them. It was told to translate faithfully, keep the option letters and their order, not solve the question and not add or remove information (translation prompt version 2976d0f96197).

The flags

In a separate request, the same model was shown each Turkish question, its English translation and the keyed option, and asked whether answering it correctly depends on Turkish wording, with the reasons (flag prompt version 08a5c70222aa). It flagged 109 of the 656 questions; they are left out, and 547 are kept. By reason, as a flagged question can have several:

  • word or phrase meaning: 76
  • idiom: 44
  • sound: 5
  • marked words: 55
  • other: 13

No person checked the translations or the flags, and this is a limit of the method: a translation error, or a question whose answer still depends on Turkish wording that the model did not flag, would stay among the 547 kept questions and could move a setup's accuracy in English. Both prompts in full are in english-reading.json and runner/translate_reading.py.

The structural check

A script (runner/translate_reading.py, its check step) then compared each translation with its Turkish original: a problem is a missing translation, option letters other than the original's, an empty text or a different count of underline markup; a warning is a change in the numbering or the numbers, Turkish letters in the English, or an English text under half or over 2.5 times the Turkish length. It found problems in 1 question (3043), already left out by the flags, so it left out no further question; its 159 warnings leave out nothing. In all, the checks left out 109 of the 656 questions and kept 547: their IDs are in kept-question-ids.txt, one per line, and in english-reading.json.

Why the grammar questions are not translated

The Text tab's 1,542 grammar questions test Turkish grammar itself, so a translation would test something else, not the same question in another language. Only the 656 reading questions were translated.

Asking the decision models

Each decision model is asked exactly as on the Text tab, with its own settings, one question per request, and with its option probabilities, except for one word of the System One instructions, the options heading and the question itself. The Text tab's instructions:

Which option is the correct answer to this Turkish multiple-choice question?

The English runs' instructions:

Which option is the correct answer to this English multiple-choice question?

The options follow the heading “Options:” instead of “Seçenekler:”, and the question and its options are the English translation. Prompt version 47f5776e71db; every English run used the translations with SHA-256 bf0d47cd385a93050c65906977e199ef7e45d5848dbbdef2bc8d124f4d5abf68. Liquid d1 was asked as d1, while its Turkish runs used d1:free, because Liquid's API no longer serves that name; its model list still names d1, released 29 September 2026. Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2 (local GPU), Perplexity Decider Flash v1.2 and Fastino GLiDE v1.2 made their Text tab runs on an NVIDIA DGX Spark and their English runs on our RTX PRO 6000 GPU, with the same checkpoint, server code and settings. Celeris-1 Decision was added on 3 November 2026 with one English run, although its repeated Turkish runs changed answers, for which the rule under Runs gives five.

Asking the chat models

Each chat model setup is asked as its Text tab run was, with the same settings (reasoning, and 16 questions per request for 26 and 1 question per request for 10), and with the Text tab's chat prompts in English: the system prompt and the instruction that ask for each answer's letter with a confidence score between 0 and 1, the question header and the options heading “Options:”. A chat model gives no option probabilities, so its confidence score is the one it stated. The English runs' system prompt:

You are taking an English multiple-choice benchmark. Select exactly one supplied option per question and state your confidence in each answer. Do not explain.

Their instruction:

Answer each of the following multiple-choice questions. Without explanation, return for each question the letter of the correct option together with a confidence score between 0 and 1 showing how sure you are that your answer is correct, in the specified JSON format.

Chat prompt version 5c3a4849752e; the Text tab's Turkish prompts are under The instructions of each kind of run. The chat models' runs with an “I don't know” option are under Our method with an “I don't know” option.

Runs

One English run per setup; five where the setup's whole-bank Turkish repeats on the Text tab changed answers. Here: five runs for Liquid d1-ultra, Perplexity Decider 27B v1, Liquid d1.1, Liquid d1, Jev 1.14.0, Drex 2.0, Jev 1.13.0, SubQ Snap Preview, Inception Mercury Decide, Microsoft-Decision-1 and Qwen3.8-27B (yes/no scoring, 1 per request); one for the other 62. The English runs are kept out of the leaderboard and its repeats.

The comparison

On the 547 kept questions only: accuracy is the right answers over 547 for the first English run and for the Text tab run (an invalid answer counts as not right), and the difference is how many points higher the English run scored than the Turkish one (negative where Turkish is higher). The paired test is the exact McNemar test on the questions only one of the two runs got right, with p adjusted by Holm's method over all 73 English setups, decision and chat alike, whatever the group shown. Where a side has more than one run, its range is the lowest and highest accuracy over its runs, and its answers changed are the kept questions whose answer differs between them.

Why the translations are not published

The site never publishes question text, Turkish or English: the publisher owns the questions. english-reading.json holds instead each reading question's ID, unit, whether it was kept, its flag reasons and the SHA-256 of its English text, with the translator and both prompts, so that a copy of these translations can be checked against it. Translating again with runner/translate_reading.py need not give the same text word for word.

The instructions of each kind of run

Each decision model run's System One instructions in full, and each chat model run's system prompt and instruction, as results.json and answers.json give them; a chat model's run with the option keeps the system prompt of its five-option run. The question and its options follow in the run's language; their text is not published.

Our method with an “I don't know” option

The option

As on the Hallucination tab, each question gets a sixth option after its own five: F, “I don't know” in English, “Bilmiyorum” in Turkish. It is always the last option, never shuffled and never correct. The English reading instructions of a decision model get one added sentence: “If you do not know the answer, choose I don't know.” The full instructions:

Which option is the correct answer to this English multiple-choice question? If you do not know the answer, choose I don't know.

Prompt version 413d6775fc58. The question and its options are the English translation, as in the accuracy comparison above; no person checked the translations. The Turkish side uses the Hallucination tab's prompts unchanged.

A chat model is asked with the chat models' English prompts, the option after each question's own and one sentence added at the end of each instruction: “If you do not know the answer, choose I don't know.” Its system prompt and instruction when it states a confidence:

You are taking an English multiple-choice benchmark. Select exactly one supplied option per question and state your confidence in each answer. Do not explain.

Answer each of the following multiple-choice questions. Without explanation, return for each question the letter of the correct option together with a confidence score between 0 and 1 showing how sure you are that your answer is correct, in the specified JSON format. If you do not know the answer, choose I don't know.

Chat prompt version e53d4aa27643. Its Turkish side uses the Hallucination tab's chat prompts unchanged.

The rates and how to read them

Each answer is right, wrong, the option or invalid. Out of the 547 kept questions, accuracy is right / 547; Answered is (right + wrong) / 547, the share of questions the model answered (the attempt rate), higher is better; Wrong of answers is wrong / (right + wrong), the share of its answers that were wrong, lower is better, and Not measured when it answered none. These two lead the table, with their counts under them. The non-hallucination rate, after them, is the option / (the option + wrong): among the answers that were not right, the share where the model said it did not know. As the Hallucination tab says, it is not a direct measure of what the model does not know: a model that always chose the option would reach 100% with no right answers, so read it with the attempt rate. With neither a wrong answer nor the option, the rate is undefined (No rate). The mean probability is the probability the model gave the option, averaged over its answers that report option probabilities; a chat model reports none. The paired test is the exact McNemar test on the questions only one of the two first runs got wrong, with p adjusted by Holm's method over the 30 decision models and the 27 chat models, each group a family of its own. No new combined score is made from these rates.

Our method with “I don't know” in both languages

What is the same

In both languages the sixth option, F, is written “I don't know”, always the last option, never shuffled and never correct, and the instructions get the same added sentence: “If you do not know the answer, choose I don't know.” Both sides are counted on the same 547 kept questions.

What differs

The language of the question and its options (the English translation, as in the accuracy comparison above, against the Turkish original); the one word of the instructions that names the language of the question; and the options heading, “Seçenekler:” against “Options:”. The instructions of the Turkish runs:

Which option is the correct answer to this Turkish multiple-choice question? If you do not know the answer, choose I don't know.

The instructions of the English runs:

Which option is the correct answer to this English multiple-choice question? If you do not know the answer, choose I don't know.

The runs

The Turkish side is the Hallucination tab's option-word run (the option's word) on all 2,198 Turkish questions, counted on the 547 kept questions only: Liquid d1-ultra (run 511), Fastino GLiDE v1.2 (run 525), Mammoth-1 (run 519), vLLM-SR d3 (run 544), Drex Max v1 (run 542), vLLM-SR d3-ultra (run 540), Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2 (local GPU) (run 531), Drex Max 1.1 (run 513), SubQ Snap 1.1 (run 512) and Elephant-1 (run 515). The English side is the first English run with “I don't know” of the section above: Liquid d1-ultra (run 449), Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2 (API, with web) (run 644), Fastino GLiDE v1.2 (run 523), Mammoth-1 (run 505), vLLM-SR d3 (run 793), Drex Max v1 (run 798), vLLM-SR d3-ultra (run 795), Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2 (local GPU) (run 529), Drex Max 1.1 (run 447), Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2 (API) (run 643), Liquid d1 (run 445), Clef (run 785), OneJev 27B (run 780), Jev 1.14.0 (run 446), SubQ Snap 1.1 (run 448), Inception Mercury Decide (run 450), Microsoft-Decision-1 (run 451), Elephant-1 (run 501), Open-Jev 27B v1.1 (run 763), Celeris-1 Decision (run 548), GPT-6 Luna (Decisions API) (run 444), Cygnet (run 755), Winnow-12B (run 748), Clef-flash (run 660), Perplexity Decider Flash v1.2 (run 535), Metask-Jev 4B (run 741), Liquid d1-2B (open weights) (run 710), Strands Decider 2B (run 704), Laya (run 728), GLiNER2.5-multi-Decide (run 716) and Laya multilingual (run 734). Their other side and paired columns read Not measured; they are in no paired test and no Holm adjustment.

The test

A wrong answer is a valid choice other than “I don't know” that is not right. The paired test is the exact McNemar test on the questions only one of the two runs got wrong, with p adjusted by Holm's method over the 10 models with both runs: a family of its own, separate from every other family on the site. The comparison with “Bilmiyorum” in Turkish stays as published in the section above (its table).

Languages the model cards list

Of the 19 models whose cards or docs we checked, only Elephant-1 and Mammoth-1 name a language: English, by the card's language: en tag. Jev's docs call English its primary language. No card names Turkish. Not checked yet, of the English setups: Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2 (API, with web), Perplexity Decider 27B v1, Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2 (API), Liquid d1.1, OneJev 27B, Drex 2.0, Jev 1.13.0, SubQ Snap Preview, Open-Jev 27B v1.1, Cygnet, Winnow-12B, Clef-flash, Metask-Jev 4B, Liquid d1-2B (open weights), meraGPT Decider 1, Strands Decider 2B, Laya, GLiNER2.5-multi-Decide, Laya multilingual and the 36 chat model setups.
